statement:
A right-angled triangle has vertices at $(2,3)$, $(9,-1)$ and $(5,k)$.

Find the sum of all the possible values of $k$.
solution:
Let $A=(2,3)$, $B=(9,-1)$, $C=(5,k)$. The right angle can be at any of the three vertices.

**Right angle at $A$:** vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}=(7,-4)$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=(3,k-3)$ are perpendicular, so
$$7\cdot3+(-4)(k-3)=0 \Rightarrow 21-4k+12=0 \Rightarrow k=\tfrac{33}{4}.$$

**Right angle at $B$:** vectors $\overrightarrow{BA}=(-7,4)$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=(-4,k+1)$ are perpendicular, so
$$(-7)(-4)+4(k+1)=0 \Rightarrow 28+4k+4=0 \Rightarrow k=-8.$$

**Right angle at $C$:** vectors $\overrightarrow{CA}=(-3,3-k)$ and $\overrightarrow{CB}=(4,-1-k)$ are perpendicular, so
$$(-3)(4)+(3-k)(-1-k)=0 \Rightarrow -12-(3-k)(1+k)=0.$$
Expanding, $-12-(3+2k-k^2)=0$, i.e. $k^2-2k-15=0$, so $(k-5)(k+3)=0$, giving $k=5$ or $k=-3$.

The possible values of $k$ are $\tfrac{33}{4}$, $-8$, $5$, $-3$. Their sum is
$$\tfrac{33}{4}+(-8)+5+(-3)=\tfrac{33}{4}-6=\tfrac{33-24}{4}=\tfrac94=2.25,$$
which is **option E**.

hints: The right angle can be at any of the three vertices.
For each case, use the dot product of two side vectors set to zero.
Collect all k values and add them.
